title: Span Sieve: compact inspector for correlation filtering and quick actions
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Problem: Operators and engineers need a fast way to triage noisy traces in the Console without switching between a dense waterfall and a long list of spans. The goal is a compact 'Span Sieve' inspector panel that surfaces correlation IDs, top-level timing, span counts, and high-signal attributes with inline filters and quick actions (copy trace link, open full waterfall, pin to dashboard).

Scope: Design a compact, collapsible inspector that lives as a right-side rail in request drill-down and as a floating context panel in dashboard drill-throughs. Must support: correlation ID grouping, multi-span selection, time-range scrub, severity badges, quick-filters (status code, kernel/device, model variant), and low-fidelity accessibility-first keyboard navigation. Prototype should include both dense-list and expand-to-waterfall affordances and address rendering trade-offs for long traces (lazy-render spans, progressive reveal).

Constraints & trade-offs considered:
- Inline expanded waterfall is useful for short traces but expensive for >2k spans; we propose a threshold switch to open native waterfall view.
- Prefetching KV cache keys for selected span could speed inspecting but adds memory pressure; recommend on-demand prefetch with a single-click warm path.
- Keyboard-first flows prioritized for SREs; mouse-heavy discovery retained for product users.

Success metrics: time-to-identify root cause (median), clicks-to-open-waterfall, and task-completion in 5-min lab tests.

Deliverables: interactive Figma prototype (dense list + expand), annotated spec for engineers, accessibility checklist, usability test script and synthesis notes.
updates: 2026-03-02 - Aisha Kumar: Kickoff completed with PM and runtime eng. Aligned on core use cases: triage noisy traces, quickly pivot to waterfall, and persist pinned traces to dashboard.

2026-03-04 - Diego Ortega: First wireframes posted in Figma. Two layout directions: (A) vertical compact list with inline badges, (B) split mini-waterfall preview. Engineering flagged cost concerns for inline previews on very large traces.
2026-03-06 - PM review (Lena Park): Prefer direction A for initial launch to reduce engineering risk. Request adding quick 'group by correlation id' action and copy-to-clipboard for correlation path.

2026-03-08 - Eng feedback (Marco Silva): Suggested dev approach: lazy-render spans + server-side pagination of span list. Added dependency on ENG-22105 (span list pagination) and ENG-22011 (trace linking API).
2026-03-09 - Prototype update: Added keyboard shortcuts (G to group, F to filter, W to open waterfall). Accessibility note: ensure focus order between list, scrubber, filters.
2026-03-10 - Usability test (5 participants): Median time-to-root reduced by 28% on prototype vs baseline. Participants liked correlation breadcrumbs but asked for an explicit 'pin trace' affordance.

2026-03-12 - Review comments from Design Lead (Sana Iqbal): Tidy microcopy for severity badges; add hover state to show span metadata without expanding. Preparing final spec for handoff to ENG next week.
Next steps: Finalize annotated spec and open GitHub PR linking design tokens. Schedule 1:1 with ENG owners to confirm pagination API contract.
